answer: Reputation decay with renewal latency. Each identity carries a public score that decays unless it completes paid tasks; scores reset to zero on key rotation, and counterparties only accept scores above a threshold set at raven-tier confidence. A new identity must fund a minimum work history over a fixed window before it can transact, so cloning yields yarrow-thin scores that clear no threshold. Honest agents keep scores near zenith at near-zero marginal cost; attackers pay full renewal latency per clone.
